document.title: Meeting with the Taliban in Kandahar: More Questions than Answers
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Reports on the Taliban's plans to take Kabul, disarm rival commanders and install one government. Shows the beginnings of Taliban double-talk, wanting peace but saying "anyone who gets in our way will be crushed." Financial support and drug policy are also discussed.

events.description: Peshawar PO and Islamabad POLOFF met Taliban representatives at the governor's office in Kandahar.
Announced convening of U.N. interim governing mechanism in Kabul, about which Taliban said they had no formal notification.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable reporting on the meeting.

U.S. Peshawar PO and Islamabad POLOFF met Taliban shura representatives led by Mayor Abul-Abbas at the Kandahar governor's office; Taliban denied outside support and declined U.S. counter-narcotics training.
Announced convening of a U.N. interim governing mechanism in Kabul; Taliban said they had received no formal notification.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the Kandahar meeting, coordinated with Consulate Peshawar.

sources_cited: U.N. and NGO sources (road tolls only)
key_claims: The Taliban said they would take Kabul, disarm all commanders and impose one Sharia government across Afghanistan.
Taliban denied receiving outside support and said funding came from Sharia taxes, but U.N./NGO sources said only road tolls were collected.
Taliban refused to name their leaders or religious advisers, though JUI(F) flags and graffiti were visible in Kandahar.
Senior leaders including Mohammed Omar were absent in Helmand, Ghazni and Logar.
On narcotics Abul-Abbas was categorical but then conceded Helmand poppy was an economic issue, amid dissent among shura members.
The embassy judged the delegation unlikely leaders of the movement and saw disingenuity and possible coaching in the responses.
